summary: This article explains how robots help in hospitals by assisting surgeons, delivering supplies, killing germs, and connecting faraway doctors with patients, while people still make the decisions and give the care.
introduce: Read the title “Robots in Hospitals” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a person who is getting care from a doctor or nurse
exact and careful, with no mistakes
to carry something to a person or place

challengeTerms.def: a control station with screens and handles used to operate a machine
a cut made on purpose, especially by a surgeon
able to act or move without someone controlling it

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that one day, robots will do most of the work in hospitals? Use evidence from the article to explain.
The article says robots cannot replace the people who work in hospitals. Do you agree?
struggling: Pre-teach patient, precise, and deliver with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use console, incision, and autonomous in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
